## Design

### 2026-10-13 – Designed the main enclosure!

**7h**

Designed the main enclosure!
My objective is to design a robust, custom 3D-printable enclosure for the MAIN_WATERING electronic assembly developed in Week 1. Rather than using traditional GUI-based CAD, I chose a parametric modeling approach using OpenSCAD since thats what i have used before.
Design Requirements & Specifications
The enclosure is engineered specifically around the layout constraints of the smart watering PCB:
Enclosure Architecture: A two-piece clamshell design (top and bottom shell) featuring a uniform wall thickness of 2.0mm for optimal structural rigidity.
PCB Positioning: Internal corner standoffs support the PCB at a height of Z=1.595mm, leaving 3.0mm of bottom clearance underneath for traces and soldering joints.
Component Clearance & Cutouts:
Pin Header (J1): Precisely aligned clearance cutout at coordinate (157.5,-82.5,1.595)mm.
Tactile Push Buttons (SW_PUSH_6mm): Mapped housing cutouts for button access at:
Push Button 1: (157.75,-108.75,1.595)mm
Push Button 2: (177.0,-111.5,1.595)mm
Push Button 3: (170.5,-111.5,1.595)mm
Fasteners: Corner screw bosses designed for M3 brass heat-set threaded inserts in the bottom shell, paired with countersunk top-lid screw holes.
CAD Modeling Workflow (OpenSCAD)
Using OpenSCAD allowed me to treat the enclosure parametrically, making adjustments to wall thicknesses, clearances, and tolerances straightforward.
// Key parameters from the model script
wall = 2.0;               // Uniform wall thickness (mm)
clearance = 0.5;          // Internal fit clearance (mm)
pcb_t = 1.595;            // PCB reference height (mm)
standoff_h = 3.0;         // Bottom clearance for traces/soldering (mm)

The script modularizes the assembly into bottom_shell(), top_shell(), and a reference pcb_assembly() module to visually verify clearance before exporting STL files for 3D printing.
Next Steps
Modell the node enclosure + bottle holder.

### 2026-10-14 – Finally finished the OpenSCAD parametric design for the node watering enclosure, and it's so much more than just a simple box—it integrates a full wall-mounting system and a 1.5L water bottle adapter!

**10h**

Finally finished the OpenSCAD parametric design for the node watering enclosure, and it's so much more than just a simple box—it integrates a full wall-mounting system and a 1.5L water bottle adapter!
The main engineering hurdle here wasn't just fitting the PCB inside a 755530mm space with 2.5mm walls, but figuring out how to mount an upside-down 1.5L water bottle directly onto the lid without creating a vacuum lock. If you screw a sealed bottle onto a flat surface, a vacuum immediately forms inside, stopping the water from flowing out.
Here is how I tackled building and solving this in the OpenSCAD script:
Enclosure & Structural Base (enclosure_base): Set up a rounded box structure with M3 PCB corner standoffs (post_radius = 3.5), side connector cutouts (J1 and J2), and a rear thermal slot for power components like Q1 and D1.
Wall Mounting Tabs (mounting_tabs): Added integrated side tabs with 3.0mm thickness and 4.0mm clearance holes (for M4 screws) so the entire node can be securely mounted to a garden post or wall.
The 1.5L Bottle Adapter & Vacuum-Breaker (enclosure_lid): Designed a central lid featuring a water outflow hole (r=8) surrounded by a robust bottle collar (38mm outer diameter, 16mm height). To solve the vacuum problem, I carved a precise air intake channel (cube([3, ...])) directly through the collar wall. This allows air to bubble up into the bottle as water drains out, keeping the gravity-fed watering system flowing smoothly! At first i though i would just drill a hole into the top of the bottle but i feel like that would be a lazy fix thats i why ended up engineering this system which did take a lot of time, hence the hours.
The tl;dr is that I built a complete system combining the electronics enclosure, M4 wall-mounting tabs, and a vacuum-compensated 1.5L bottle adapter into a single, clean OpenSCAD script ready for slicing.
Time spent this session: 10 hours

### 2026-10-14 – Integrated a slide-in wall mount into the remote node enclosure!

**2h**

Integrated a slide-in wall mount into the remote node enclosure!

I wanted to make sure the physical setup  was actually practical to maintain. Screwing an enclosure directly to a surface makes changing batteries or checking wiring a massive pain.
Here is how I tackled designing and coding these new features into the OpenSCAD script:

The Simple Slide-In Mount (wall_mounting_bracket): Ditched the old fixed side tabs entirely. Instead, I added a separate wall bracket and a matching rectangular slot cut directly into the back wall of the base. Now, you can anchor the small bracket to a garden post once with an M4 screw, and the entire enclosure simply slides downward onto it for tool-free removal.
tl;dr: replaced fixed screw tabs with a clean, easy-to-print slide-in wall mount system.
Time spent this session: 2 hours

### 2026-10-15 – Overview

**8h**

Overview
This development session finalizes the complete production-ready CAD package for the DripLogic Node Watering system. By expanding the modular plumbing library and introducing an integrated inline valve manifold, the design achieves full fluid-path versatility while maintaining strict environmental isolation for the core electronics.
Key Architectural Updates
Sealed Wet/Dry Separation:
The main enclosure base and flat solid lid utilize a tongue-and-groove lap joint with friction crush-ribs, ensuring a completely sealed dry zone for the control board.
The side-mounted bottle caddy (side_caddy) isolates the 1.5L PET reservoir (optimized for standard Xixo bottle necks at 28.5 mm diameter) away from electronics, featuring an offset threaded outflow and a separate 4.3 mm breather snorkel hole.
Expanded Hollow Plumbing Library:
All fittings feature a standardized internal water bore diameter of 10.0 mm (water_bore_d) to ensure unrestricted fluid flow.
Added modular connectivity options including straight, curved, and 90-degree elbow hollow water path connectors (straight_fitting, curve_fitting, elbow90_fitting).
Introduced female coupling sockets (female_fitting) and extended double-female tubes (female_tube_long) for flexible assembly configurations.
Advanced Solenoid Integration & Output Controls:
Solenoid Inline Valve (solenoid_inline_valve): A newly engineered flow-control manifold featuring horizontal male threading, a direct internal water pass-through bore, and a vertical 1/2" threaded top port designed specifically for the WSV-12V solenoid plunger to drop down and block the water path.
Sprinkler End Cap (sprinkler_fitting): A termination fitting equipped with a female thread, a tapered reduction nozzle, and a radial array of angled holes for optimized garden bed distribution.
Production Layout
All primary enclosures, brackets, holders, and specialized fittings are organized cleanly within the print_plate render module, configured for multi-part batch printing.
